anchor.statement: Lemma 8.6. Let N = v t · ∂y on T2 , with v t as in (6.2), and let F be a smooth function of zero Haar mean. Then N φ = F has a unique smooth zero-mean solution φ = N −1 F. This solution is given by the following Fourier series and satisfies the displayed norm bound for every integer m ≥ 0: N −1 F = ∑ k∈ Z 2 \{0} ˆ︁ F(k) 2 π iv t · k e 2 π ik·y , ∥N −1 F∥ Cm y ≤ C m ∥F∥ C m+4 y . (8.19) For a pair E θ , E z ∈ M α of normalized angularly invariant residual coefficients, use this inverse in the original auxiliary coordinate Y to define the physical tangential update −N −1 abs (E ◦ θ ,phys , E ◦ z,phys ). correspondence.note: The derivative loss differs: (8.19) states ‖N⁻¹F‖_{C^m_y} ≤ C_m‖F‖_{C^{m+4}_y}, while inverse_finiteJets states JetBound f S (n + 5) C → JetBound (inverse d f) S n (K * C), i.e. bounds on all derivatives of order ≤ n+5 (parameter and torus jointly) give bounds of order ≤ n, a loss of five derivatives rather than four. The solution, its zero mean, uniqueness per torus slice, the Mα class of the increments and the update (8.20)–(8.22) are stated by the other declarations.
